extracted.intended_audience: photography teachers, visual literacy educators, and educational researchers interested in using photography therapeutically
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and standards for using photography as a therapeutic and holistic educational tool—how to design assignments, pedagogical posture, and curricular integration to promote right-hemispheric/intuitive development and personal growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography as therapy (conceptual justification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Photography as therapy, a useful concept for advocates of humanistic education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat photography not only as a communication medium but as a therapeutic activity that helps individuals externalize and examine internal feelings; position it within a holistic educational perspective rather than as a narrow vocational skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography as a carrier of ideas and emotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Like writing and speaking, image-making is a carrier of ideas... as a language, it is particularly adapted to description, bringing together holistically, concepts about subjects that would require long linear chains of written or spoken words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use photographs to convey complex, holistic meanings and to arouse immediate emotional responses; favor images that sum up total properties of a concept rather than rely on lengthy verbal explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use photography to access right-hemispheric (intuitive/holistic) functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Photography as therapy concerns itself about those ideas that we hold as unique individuals and is particularly connected to right-hemispheric intuition, holism, and spatial perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design photographic experiences that encourage intuitive, holistic perception (similar to meditation) to balance analytical, left-hemispheric emphasis in conventional schooling; view photography as a means to develop intuition and holistic judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate photography across the curriculum to promote balanced thinkers
rubrics_metrics.description: To promote 'balanced thinkers'... educational activities (such as photography) need to be integrated with the rest of the school curriculum, resulting in more-complete individuals functioning in harmony with their environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed photography into subjects (history, social studies, reading) rather than isolating it; curricular integration is recommended to counteract an educational imbalance favoring analytic skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer non-directed, personally meaningful photographic assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of photography should be non-directed: only broad parameters might be employed such as 'photograph your family or your neighborhood,' to encourage the photographer to become personally involved and absorbed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid highly prescriptive tasks; give broad prompts that allow students to choose personally meaningful subjects so the images reflect inner feelings and personal engagement—this maximizes therapeutic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use photographs as feedback for self-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Looking at these images with the attitudes of images as carriers of certain kinds of ideas that relate in a personal way to the individual, serves as resource for feedback for self-analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruct students to reflect on and discuss their images as a means of self-understanding; structure reflective viewing sessions to elicit personal meaning rather than only technical critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing images as a therapeutic and cross-cultural bridge
rubrics_metrics.description: An important and often overlooked aspect of making images is the desire to share them. The photograph becomes a bridge in which diverse cultural backgrounds can meet and develop understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate sharing and discussion of students' photographs to foster empathy, cultural exchange, and mutual understanding; use sharing to surface issues teachers can help address or refer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher role: visual listener and referral agent (not therapist)
rubrics_metrics.description: A trained teacher can discover and open doorways to possible solutions of students’ personal problems. The teacher... can, in any event, become a friend, a visual listener, so to speak, and in some instances, direct the student to other, more qualified persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers should adopt a listening, supportive stance when using photography therapeutically, recognize limits of their expertise, and refer students to trained therapists when necessary; avoid practicing clinical therapy unless qualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rote/survey teaching that kills intrinsic motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: You can kill this off by offering a survey course in photography and having students memorize dates and places. Kids develop a negative reaction to a lot of teaching--a fear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor experiential, skill-developing, and personally meaningful instruction over memorization and purely historical/survey approaches; preserve joy and intrinsic motivation in photographic learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage presence/flow to produce unique personal photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: The moment of creation in photography is similar to a state of consciousness very much sought after in yoga... if a photographer can become sufficiently aware of this continuum and have the energy to push a shutter when inside and outside click together, that camera might produce some very fine photographs indeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design activities and classroom cultures that promote focused, absorbed attention ('flow') so students can produce original work reflecting a unique personal viewpoint; encourage mindfulness and awareness during image-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography as tool to foster holistic problem-solving at societal level
rubrics_metrics.description: We have, in fact, utilized the capacities of our left hemisphere... that we have lost sight of the holistic overall consequences of our actions... It is only with great effort that environmentalists find it possible to control the irrational destruction of our natural resources, becoming, in fact, a battle between the holistic overview as opposed to the linear, analytical...needs of an industrial society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use photographic education to cultivate holistic thinking that can be applied to environmental and societal problems; teach students to see broader contexts and consequences, not merely analytical segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational programs must recognize individuality and moral development
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs must recognize the uniqueness, human-ness and individuality of the student... the commitment of education is finally... a commitment to the individual, to his total capabilities as a human being... not only to his abilities to analyze but to...intuition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design curricula that honor individual development, moral values, and the cultivation of intuition alongside analytic skills; position photography education as contributing to the formation of the 'total person.'
